description: We are space enthusiasts bridging the gap between hard science and interactive storytelling. By combining open NASA datasets with rapid game prototyping in Godot 4, our goal is to prove that raw scientific telemetry can be the foundation for immersive, psychological gameplay
summary: Al Ghaib ("the unseen") is a 2D survival-horror game that turns real NASA data into gameplay. After a disease spreads through a crew on a pilgrimage to TRAPPIST-1 f, two untouched crew members have one month to find a cure. In Mission 1, Zayd enters a dark cave to collect a Bacillus subtilis sample while an unseen, freezing presence hunts him. His tablet shows planet values from the NASA Exoplanet Archive and the sample's study, OSD-185, from NASA's Open Science Data Repository. Opening the tablet leaves him blind and frozen, so every use is a risk, and frost on the screen warns how close the creature is. Players repair damaged radio messages with a parity-check puzzle, inspired by error correction in space communication, and sequence the sample's DNA before it degrades. The game makes players manage oxygen, time and communication under mission constraints. It matters because most people never open NASA's science archives, and here they meet real data by playing.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: Al Ghaib is a 2D horror platformer made in Godot. The player controls Zayd, who explores a cave on TRAPPIST-1 f with a mouse-aimed flashlight. An invisible creature chases him and retreats from light, but it can only hurt him while his tablet is open, because the tablet blinds and freezes him. The tablet shows planet values from the NASA Exoplanet Archive and the sample's details from NASA OSDR study OSD-185. Players solve a 5x5 parity-check puzzle to repair a damaged radio message, collect a Bacillus subtilis sample, and sequence a practice DNA strand (A-T, C-G pairing) before the sample degrades. Oxygen and health bars add mission pressure.

IMPACT: Most people never open NASA's science archives. The game lets them play with the data and learn how error correction and spaceflight biology work.

TOOLS: Godot 4.7 (GDScript), GitHub, Gemini for image generation, Claude for coding and planning help.

CREATIVITY: Fear comes from the interface. The only way to get answers also makes the player helpless, and frost on the screen is the only warning.

FACTORS: We loaded NASA values from files taken from the NASA pages, and cite them. The DNA strand is a gameplay puzzle, not study data. The timers and creature behavior are our own design, not NASA figures.
